resolved_label: BONNIE ST. JOHN, AUTHOR, "HOW GREAT WOMEN LEAD"
text: I lost my leg when I was five and I've had a prosthesis ever since. My heart went out when I heard so many of the victims were going to be amputees, and just wanted to see if I could help.

resolved_label: MERY DANIEL, BOSTON MARATHON BOMBING SURVIVOR
text: She's been a supportive friend and she understands how I'm going to face the world after this because my life will never be the same.

resolved_label: BONNIE ST. JOHN, AUTHOR, "HOW GREAT WOMEN LEAD"

resolved_label: SUZANNE MALVEAUX, CNN ANCHOR
text: I know that Mery Daniel is up for the challenge. Want to welcome you both. It's so great to see you guys. Bonnie St. John, joining us from Boston, Mery as well Bonnie, good to see you as well. At one point, I'm sure there was a turning point where thought, I need to be back there. I need to be down there.

resolved_label: BONNIE ST. JOHN, AUTHOR, "HOW GREAT WOMEN LEAD"
text: Well, we heard the news that so many of the people injured were going to lose limbs, and I've been trained to visit people in hospital and help them start making strides to the future. And I just wanted to come and see if I could help. So I visited a number of people. But Mery and I really made a connection, and she wasn't out there in the first weeks telling her story and raising money for her future, so I wanted to get her connected and get her story out there.

resolved_label: MICHAEL HOLMES, CNN ANCHOR
text: Mery, tell us how you have progressed, your path since this happened. Obviously it's a terrible shock. It's a terrible loss in terms of mobility and the rest. Tell us about the journey from there to now.

resolved_label: MERY DANIEL, BOSTON MARATHON BOMBING SURVIVOR
text: Well, from nearly being dead, my heart had stopped twice while the doctors at Mass General were trying to revive me. From that point on, I was unconscious for three days, and then I realized I had lost one limb and part of the other leg was all blown away. And from spending three weeks at Mass General, recovering, to now being at the rehab hospital, it's been a journey. It's a difficult one, but I've been doing it.

resolved_label: MICHAEL HOLMES, CNN ANCHOR
text: How do you feel now, though, since meeting Bonnie and seeing the remarkable progress? How is your outlook now?

resolved_label: MERY DANIEL, BOSTON MARATHON BOMBING SURVIVOR
text: Well, the support has been very beneficial, and it's been -- having support gives you a lot of strength, and that's been helping a lot. And my family is very supportive. And I have a lot of friends and people are rooting for me out there.

resolved_label: SUZANNE MALVEAUX, CNN ANCHOR
text: And, Bonnie, tell us if -- go ahead.

resolved_label: BONNIE ST. JOHN, AUTHOR, "HOW GREAT WOMEN LEAD"
text: I was going to say she took her first step a week ago with a walker. She doesn't have a prosthesis yet. And you saw the pictures of us out riding hand cycle, so a lot of progress in the last week. It's been very exciting.

resolved_label: SUZANNE MALVEAUX, CNN ANCHOR
text: Yeah, very excited for both of you. Bonnie, explain to us here because it's a different scenario. What do you think is the most challenging part about what Mery is going to be facing because your situation was different, having lost your leg as a five-year-old, just as a little girl and Mary here really in a very different place in her life. What do you think is going to be the challenge that she's really going to need to face moving forward?

resolved_label: BONNIE ST. JOHN, AUTHOR, "HOW GREAT WOMEN LEAD"
text: So many things, and I admire her courage that she has a lot more to deal with than I did. Her, quote, "good" leg is missing a lot of muscle and she had skin grafts on the back of her leg, so it's going to be a while before her good leg is really strong enough to get out and do some of the things she needs to do. She's going to have a lot of hard work and physical therapy getting strong again. And she's a mother. She has a 5-year-old daughter, so caring for her. Just the normal things we take for granted, running errands and picking up things around the house and going back to work and, you know, a lot of challenges ahead and we want to surround her with support to help her.
